subject: Cache behavior mismatch reported by Acme - API responses inconsistent
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Lowry <michael.lowry@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Cache behavior mismatch reported by Acme - initial report

Team,

Quick heads-up: Acme flagged that for a small subset of requests their inference results jump between two different tokenization/response variants even when using the same model + prompt and identical request parameters. They see this across their staging region (us-west-2) and it started after we pushed the runtime patch last week.

Summary from Michael (copied):
- Same prompt repeated 10x returns variant A 6x and variant B 4x, random-seeming.
- They see different tokenization boundaries causing short responses vs. long completions.
- Happens at ~25% of requests under burst load; not every request.

Acme is evaluating reliability before committing to Dedicated capacity. Can runtime help confirm whether KV cache / prefix caching could return stale/combine entries across concurrent shards? If this is an unintended interaction with the kernel selection changes, we need an immediate mitigation (a flag to disable prefix caching or a conservative routing pin).

I'm attaching a small sample of their logs and a reproducible script they shared. Michael — thanks for sending the samples.

Requested next steps:
- Dev: reproduce and confirm whether cache keys ever collide across sessions or routing variants.
- Jasmine: can you confirm if any recent kernel selection heuristics touched the tokenizer or attention start-index paths?
- Marissa: I'll sync with Acme on timeline and whether they'd accept a temporary rate-limit/serializing workaround.

Thanks,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0119

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Lowry <michael.lowry@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cache behavior mismatch reported by Acme - initial report

Thanks Marcus — digging in. Quick notes after a first pass on the attached logs and the repro script:

1) Repro is helpful: it hits the same model variant repeatedly and toggles concurrency from 1 -> 8. I can reproduce a high variance in response shape when concurrency > 4.
2) The KV cache is per-request-id but we do have a shared prefix cache for common prompt prefixes to save compute. That prefix cache uses a hashed key of (model, tokenizer-version, prompt-prefix, seqlen-bin).
3) I'm seeing occasional mismatches where the tokenizer-version used to compute the prefix hash is different from the tokenizer actually used at inference time after kernel re-selection. That would explain differing token boundaries while the prefix cache returns an older prefix chunk.

Proposed short-term mitigation: expose an override in the runtime config to disable prefix cache per-customer or per-route (config flag: runtime.disable_prefix_cache=true). That would avoid inconsistent cached chunks while we fix the kernel/tokenizer handshake.

Long-term: ensure tokenizer-version is wired into kernel selection and cached with the exact compiled-kernel checksum.

I'll prepare a small patch and smoke-test in staging. Michael — can you test with a route that sets 1 concurrency for the next hour while we validate?

--
Dev
Lead Platform Engineer

From: Michael Lowry <michael.lowry@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cache behavior mismatch reported by Acme - initial report

Thanks for the fast review. We ran an A/B test this morning: route A had concurrency=1 (serial), route B had concurrency=8. Route A showed stable Variant A responses; route B still had mixed variants.

We can toggle concurrency for a limited window. If you can provide the runtime flag, we'll flip it on our Dedicated trial and monitor accuracy. The attached acme_logs_sample_20260712.txt has timestamps and request IDs — let me know if you need full logs (we can share via secure link).

-Michael

Attachments: acme_logs_sample_20260712.txt

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Lowry <michael.lowry@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T12:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cache behavior mismatch reported by Acme - initial report

FYI I traced the kernel-selection patch that went out last Tuesday (rkd-2026-07-06). The change adds a fallback to an older integer-attention kernel for long sequences if the JIT sampler detects a memory pressure pattern. It does not intentionally modify tokenizer outputs, but I can see we only pass a tokenizer "version id" as metadata, not the compiled-kernel checksum. If runtime re-selects a different kernel after the prefix cache was populated, the tokenizer binary used at inference could differ in subtle ways (token boundary handling).

Action items from infra side:
- Dev: please add tokenizer-version and compiler-checksum into the prefix cache key (short patch).
- Short-term: Dev's proposal to disable prefix cache per-route looks feasible and faster to ship. I can review the change and push to staging.

Also: logging addition request — include the prefix-cache:key and kernel-checksum in our debug logs when prefix hits/misses occur. That will speed triage for other customers.

-Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Applied ML / Runtime Integrations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Lowry <michael.lowry@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T14:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cache behavior mismatch reported by Acme - initial report (next steps & customer comms)

Thanks everyone — nice quick loop. Summary and plan to share with Acme: 

1) Root cause hypothesis: prefix cache key is not sufficiently tied to the exact kernel/tokenizer binary, causing mismatched cached chunks under high concurrency when kernel re-selection occurs.
2) Short-term mitigation (<=24h): runtime team to add per-route flag runtime.disable_prefix_cache (Dev to ship smoke patch to staging today). We'll ask Acme to enable it for their trial routes while we validate accuracy.
3) Medium-term fix (1-2 weeks): include tokenizer-version + kernel-checksum in cache keys and add debug logging for cache:key and kernel:checksum on prefix hits/misses. Jasmine to lead code review.
4) Customer comms: Marcus to send a short note confirming the mitigation and proposed timeline. Marissa will own pressure on the priority tracker for Dedicated-deal risk.

Michael — we'll flag you when the staging build is ready. Appreciate your patience on this.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Cache behavior mismatch reported by Acme - initial report (customer note)

Michael — quick confirmation: runtime is rolling a staging patch now and will expose a route-level toggle to disable the prefix cache. If you enable that toggle for your trial routes we expect the inconsistent variants to disappear. We'll follow up with the staging build link and a short validation checklist (smoke requests, sample ids).

I'll also escalate to Product that this tokenizer/kernel binding is a correctness risk for Dedicated customers and recommend we prioritize the medium-term fix after the smoke window.

Thanks,
Marcus
